purpose: Quantify accessible coupling information in a declared output-field homodyne measurement.

input_output.sign_convention: plus sign; changing the input phase changes only the output phase convention
input_output.total_loss: kappa = kappa_ext + kappa_int, all normalized by wc
input_output.temporal_mode: flat f(t)=1/sqrt(tau) over [0,tau] in normalized time

solver.correlations: qutip.correlation_2op_2t using the quantum regression theorem
solver.integration: composite trapezoid on the stored temporal mode grid
solver.gaussian_distribution: mean and variance of a single-mode Gaussian quadrature law

validation.convergence_note: Rows include finite-difference, mode-resolution, window, phase, efficiency, external-coupling, and cavity-truncation scans; this is a bounded screen, not an asymptotic convergence proof.

caveats: CFI is computed for a Gaussian moment-based quadrature approximation, not the exact generally non-Gaussian temporal-mode distribution.
The output mode includes the explicit vacuum shot-noise variance but does not reconstruct the full continuum output state or detector bandwidth chain.
The primary QFI comparator is the fidelity QFI of the reconstructed Gaussian output-mode state; the residual cavity-qubit QFI is retained as a separate diagnostic.
The input-output mapping treats only kappa_ext as monitored; internal loss is not measurable output.
The flat temporal mode is a declared analysis choice, not an optimized matched filter.
The calculation does not establish experimental QFI saturation, universal homodyne optimality, or resource-normalized advantage.
